focus.description: Maintaining a high click rate requires short-window focus and physical pacing. Pushing through the 5s or 10s mode tests how consistently you can maintain your rhythm without locking up.

neural.description: Measures physical tapping speed and finger control. Rapid clicking tests your hand muscles' ability to execute fast, repetitive keystrokes with minimal wasted motion.

science.title: What a CPS Test Actually Measures
science.description: A CPS test serves as a physical benchmark for mouse clicking speed. It measures burst motor output, finger tapping rhythm, and short-window mechanical pacing across standardized 1s, 3s, 5s, and 10s intervals.
science.blogArticleTitle: Read: What Is a Good CPS Score?

focus.question: Is this just about hand speed?
focus.answer: It primarily measures clicking speed over a short interval. Attention, technique, device latency, and hand fatigue can all affect a score, so it should not be treated as a standalone measure of concentration.

warmup.question: Is this a good pre-game warm-up?
warmup.answer: It can be used as a brief physical warm-up or equipment check. Keep attempts short, use a comfortable grip, and stop if you feel pain or strain.

improve.question: How to improve my score?
improve.answer: Use the same device and duration when comparing attempts. A comfortable grip, consistent technique, and short rests can reduce fatigue; stop if repeated clicking causes discomfort.

health.question: Can high-speed clicking cause injury?
health.answer: Yes, prolonged repetition can cause fatigue. Please practice moderately in short sets and stop immediately if you feel pain. This is designed for burst training, not endurance marathons.

cpsMeaning.question: What does CPS mean?
cpsMeaning.answer: CPS stands for Clicks Per Second. A CPS test measures how many mouse clicks you can produce in a fixed amount of time, which is why it is also called a click speed test or mouse clicking test.

bestMode.question: Which mode is best: 1s, 5s, or 10s?
bestMode.answer: The 1-second mode measures burst speed, the 5-second mode is the most common standard, and the 10-second mode tests consistency. If you want a realistic benchmark, 5s and 10s are usually the most useful.
